newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sees net foreign loan outflow in July.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sees net foreign loan outflow in July.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Tuesday outstanding foreign loans tapped by Thai-based borrowers through offshore banking units fell for the first time in July after it introduced in measures to curb short-term borrowing inflows.

The central bank said outstanding out-in foreign loans imported by offshore banking units fell to 767.8 billion baht ($30.7 billion) at the end of July from 774.9 billion a month earlier. This compared with 595.4 billion a year ago.

It said total out-out offshore loans channelled through licensed banks also declined slightly to 486.9 billion baht at the end of July from 491.5 billion the previous month and against 262.4 billion a year ago.

Out-in loans are foreign borrowings brought in by offshore banking units for re-lending to Thai-based clients. Out-out loans refer to offshore funds lent to borrowers in third countries but processed by Thai-based offshore banks.

Thailand in late June started requiring offshore banking units to set aside a seven percent cash reserve on short-term foreign funds of less than one year maturity used for re-lending to local clients.

Central bank figures showed that the July decline of outstanding borrowed foreign funds could be attributed to capital outflows made through foreign bank branches and those with representative offices in Thailand.
They showed total funds borrowed through Thai banks posted a slightly increase in July.
